chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Banu Umayya allowed the people to learn faith (Iman), but they did not allow them to learn polytheism (Shirk), so that when they imposed it upon them, they would not recognize it.

key_terms.الْإِيمَان: Faith, belief in God and core tenets
key_terms.بَنُو أُمَيَّةَ: The Clan of Umayya, referring to the Umayyad dynasty

ai.seo_question: How did the Umayyads manipulate the concept of faith to maintain their rule?
ai.summary: Sufyan ibn Uyayna, a prominent early hadith scholar, highlights the Umayyad strategy of subtle theological manipulation by teaching 'Iman' while obscuring 'Shirk,' ensuring the masses accepted their rule as legitimate faith. This reflects the Shia critique of political legitimacy, where rulers often mask polytheistic deviations (such as deifying authority) within accepted religious terminology. The hadith underscores the importance of distinguishing true monotheism from political idolatry, a key theme in Shia historical analysis.
